June 15, 2026

VIA ELECTRONIC SUBMISSION

Dr. Mehmet Oz, MD, MBA
Administrator
Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services
Department of Health and Human Services
Baltimore, MD 21244-8013

RE: Medicare and Medicaid Programs; Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act; Interoperability Standards and Prior Authorization for Drugs for Medicare Advantage Organizations, Medicaid Managed Care Plans, State Medicaid Agencies, Children's Health Insurance Program (CHIP) Agencies and CHIP Managed Care Entities, and Issuers of Qualified Health Plans on the Federally-Facilitated Exchanges [CMS-0062-P]

Dear Administrator Oz:

ViiV Healthcare Company (ViiV) appreciates the opportunity to provide comments to the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) regarding Medicare and Medicaid Programs; Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act; Interoperability Standards and Prior Authorization for Drugs... An estimated 1.2 million people in the United States are living with HIV, nearly half of whom are covered by payers that could be affected by this rulemaking. A further 2.3 million people in the United States may benefit from PrEP, many of whom are also enrolled in plans that would be subject to these policies.
analysis:
## 1. COMMENTER INFORMATION

- **Author/Organization name:** ViiV Healthcare Company, signed by Carie Blackburn, Head, Government Relations & Advocacy
- **Stakeholder type:** Other (pharmaceutical manufacturer — only independent global specialist company focused exclusively on HIV treatment and prevention)
- **Credentials or expertise mentioned:** Founded 2009; singular focus on HIV treatment and prevention; developer of antiretroviral (ARV) therapies and PrEP products including long-acting injectables

---

## 2. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

ViiV Healthcare broadly supports the proposed electronic prior authorization standards and uses this comment to advocate specifically for HIV patients and those who may benefit from PrEP. ViiV urges CMS to maintain and strengthen protections against utilization management for antiretrovirals — including extending the Medicare Part D protected class prohibition across all CMS-regulated markets — and to establish a unified 24-hour PA timeframe for time-sensitive drug classes. ViiV also calls for more granular PA metrics reporting disaggregated by drug and therapeutic area, portability of prior step therapy decisions, and prohibition of PA for PrEP-related lab services.

---

## 3. REGULATORY CONTEXT

- **Specific provisions addressed:** PA-DRUG-PHARMACY, PA-DRUG-MEDICAL, PA-TIMEFRAMES-DRUGS, API-USAGE-METRICS, GENERAL, FF-SHOP-REQUIREMENTS
- **Regulatory citations mentioned:** 42 CFR Parts 422 and 423 (Part D protected classes/six protected classes); ACA preventive services mandate; USPSTF recommendation for PrEP; Tri-Department FAQs Part 68 (October 21, 2024); CMS NCD for PrEP (September 30, 2024)
- **Standards referenced:** FHIR-based Prior Authorization API; NCPDP SCRIPT (implicit for pharmacy benefit); medical benefit API for real-time coverage checks

---

## 4. DETAILED POSITIONS

**Topic 1: Maintain Part D ARV Protected Class Prohibition on Utilization Management**
- **Provision ID:** PA-DRUG-PHARMACY
- **Position:** Support (maintain existing protection)
- **Rationale:** ARVs are one of six protected classes under Medicare Part D with an additional prohibition on PA and step therapy even for new starts. HIV is highly individualized, uniquely sensitive to treatment interruptions, and requires continuous access to clinically appropriate therapy to reduce morbidity, mortality, and transmission.
- **Specific request:** CMS should maintain the Part D prohibition on utilization management for ARVs as a protected class.

**Topic 2: Strengthen Oversight of Utilization Management for PrEP**
- **Provision ID:** GENERAL
- **Position:** Modify
- **Rationale:** Despite Tri-Department FAQ Part 68 directing applicable issuers not to use utilization management to direct patients to one PrEP formulation over another, many issuers and plans continue to inappropriately apply PA to PrEP and ancillary services.
- **Specific request:** CMS should use improved reporting requirements to increase oversight over issuers applying prohibited utilization management to PrEP; standardized ePA should reduce violations.

**Topic 3: Support Finalization of Electronic PA Standards**
- **Provision ID:** PA-DRUG-MEDICAL, PA-DRUG-PHARMACY, FHIR-IG-REQUIRED
- **Position:** Support
- **Rationale:** Electronic PA standards for MA, Medicaid, and QHPs on FFEs will reduce administrative burden and access delays for ARVs.
- **Specific request:** Finalize the proposed ePA requirements.

**Topic 4: Real-Time Coverage Check to Preempt Wrong-Benefit Rejections**
- **Provision ID:** PA-DRUG-MEDICAL, MEDICAL-VS-PHARMACY-BENEFIT
- **Position:** Modify
- **Rationale:** Long-acting injectable ARVs (e.g., cabotegravir/rilpivirine) and PrEP injectables can be covered under pharmacy benefit, medical benefit, or both depending on payer, leading to wrong-benefit rejections that delay access.
- **Specific request:** (a) Require payers to provide real-time benefit routing information to providers; (b) require medical benefit PA APIs to enable patient-specific real-time coverage checks similar to pharmacy benefit RTPB capability; (c) require payers to reroute claims to the correct benefit without requiring provider resubmission where possible.

**Topic 5: Unified 24-Hour PA Timeframe; No Extensions for Time-Sensitive Drug Classes**
- **Provision ID:** PA-TIMEFRAMES-DRUGS
- **Position:** Modify
- **Rationale:** ViiV supports the proposed 72-hour standard / 24-hour expedited timeframes but urges a uniform 24-hour limit for all requests across all payer types (aligned with Medicaid FFS/managed care). For ARVs and PrEP, even brief delays cause clinical and public health harm — HHS guidelines recommend ART initiation "immediately or as soon as possible" after diagnosis; delayed PrEP dispensing of 1–7 days increases 12-month HIV acquisition risk by 20%.
- **Specific request:** Adopt uniform 24-hour decision timeframe for all utilization management requests; prohibit extensions for expedited requests for time-sensitive drug classes including ARVs.

**Topic 6: More Granular PA Metrics Reporting**
- **Provision ID:** API-USAGE-METRICS
- **Position:** Modify
- **Rationale:** Proposed reporting is insufficient to monitor whether HIV patients or other specific populations are disproportionately impacted by utilization management. Current framework cannot detect payer gaming (denial increases in response to shorter timeframes).
- **Specific request:** Require payer data disaggregated by: drug, therapeutic area, reason for denial, brand vs. generic, type of utilization management, and plan type; require reporting on prescription abandonment and non-prescribed drug substitution; require step therapy metrics disaggregated or clearly identified; CMS should analyze received data to monitor for payer gaming behavior.

**Topic 7: Prohibit PA and Step Therapy for HIV Treatment Across All CMS Markets**
- **Provision ID:** GENERAL
- **Position:** Modify
- **Rationale:** Part D ARV protected class protection should be extended to all CMS-regulated markets. PA and step therapy for stable HIV patients can force non-medical switching, which a systematic review of 29 studies linked to poor side effects, nonadherence, and negative outcomes. Six states (CO, LA, NV, NY, TX, OR) have already enacted similar protections.
- **Specific request:** (a) Prohibit PA and step therapy for HIV treatment across all CMS-regulated markets, especially for patients on stable therapy; (b) at minimum, require payers to honor prior step therapy and PA decisions when a patient changes coverage; (c) set limits on PA frequency; (d) enforce USPSTF/FAQ Part 68 prohibition on utilization management directing PrEP formulation choice.

**Topic 8: Prohibit PA for PrEP-Related Lab Services**
- **Provision ID:** GENERAL
- **Position:** Modify
- **Rationale:** PrEP requires routine HIV testing and ancillary lab services; ACA preventive services mandate requires coverage at no cost, yet some patients still pay out of pocket. PA for these lab services creates an access barrier to PrEP continuation.
- **Specific request:** Prohibit plans and issuers subject to ACA preventive services mandates from requiring PA for PrEP-related lab services; strengthen oversight of prohibited cost-sharing.

---

## 5. SOLICITATION RESPONSES

- **S14 (non-Part D pharmacy PA applicability):** ViiV supports requiring NCPDP-based ePA standards for pharmacy benefit drugs; notes long-acting injectable ARVs create benefit routing confusion needing real-time coverage check capability.
- **S15 (medical vs. pharmacy benefit distinction):** ViiV explicitly addresses this: long-acting injectable HIV products can be billed under either benefit, causing wrong-benefit PA rejections; urges real-time routing information and automatic rerouting.
- **S20 (24-hour PA timeframe achievability):** ViiV urges CMS to go further — adopt a uniform 24-hour standard for all requests, not just expedited; prohibit extensions for time-sensitive ARV/PrEP classes.
- **S43 (align timeframes):** ViiV recommends aligning all payer types to a uniform 24-hour decision timeframe consistent with Medicaid FFS/managed care.
- **S29 (which metrics to collect):** ViiV urges granular disaggregation by drug, therapeutic area, denial reason, brand vs. generic, utilization management type, plan type; include prescription abandonment and non-prescribed drug substitution.
- **S35 (publish aggregate metrics):** ViiV urges CMS to use data to actively monitor for payer gaming (increased denials in response to shorter timeframes).
- **S68 (step therapy RFI):** ViiV urges prohibition of PA and step therapy for HIV treatment across all CMS markets; portability of prior determinations; frequency limits on PA; enforcement of PrEP UM prohibition.
- **S70 (laboratory tests RFI):** ViiV urges prohibition of PA for PrEP-related lab services for issuers subject to ACA preventive services mandates; strengthen oversight of prohibited cost-sharing.

---

## 6. RECOMMENDATIONS

1. Maintain the Medicare Part D prohibition on utilization management for ARVs as one of the six protected classes.
2. Finalize the proposed ePA requirements for MA, Medicaid, and QHPs on FFEs.
3. Strengthen oversight of payers inappropriately applying utilization management to PrEP.
4. Require payers to provide real-time benefit routing information to allow providers to determine pharmacy vs. medical benefit coverage for each patient.
5. Require medical benefit PA APIs to support patient-specific real-time coverage checks similar to pharmacy benefit RTPB capability.
6. Require payers to reroute wrong-benefit claims without requiring provider resubmission where possible.
7. Adopt a uniform 24-hour decision timeframe for all utilization management requests across all applicable payer types.
8. Prohibit payers from extending expedited request timeframes for time-sensitive drug classes including ARVs.
9. Require PA metrics disaggregated by drug, therapeutic area, denial reason, brand vs. generic, utilization management type, and plan type.
10. Require reporting on prescription abandonment and cases where patients received a different drug than initially prescribed.
11. Require step therapy metrics disaggregated or clearly identified within PA data.
12. CMS should analyze received data to monitor for payer gaming (increased denials in response to shorter timeframes).
13. Prohibit PA and step therapy for HIV treatment across all CMS-regulated markets, especially for patients on stable therapy.
14. Require payers to honor prior step therapy and PA decisions when patients change coverage.
15. Set limits on PA frequency.
16. Enforce USPSTF/Tri-Department FAQ Part 68 prohibition on utilization management directing PrEP formulation choice.
17. Prohibit plans subject to ACA preventive services mandates from requiring PA for PrEP-related lab services.

---

## 7. CONCERNS & OBJECTIONS

- **Primary concerns:** PA, step therapy, and non-medical switching barriers to HIV treatment and PrEP access; ongoing violation of PrEP UM prohibitions despite existing guidance; wrong-benefit rejections for long-acting injectables; insufficient PA metrics granularity to detect population-level harms.
- **Potential negative impacts cited:** 20% increased HIV acquisition risk from 1–7 day PrEP dispensing delay; non-medical ARV switching associated with poor side effects, nonadherence, and negative outcomes; delayed ART initiation increases morbidity, mortality, and HIV transmission risk.
- **Implementation barriers mentioned:** Benefit routing ambiguity for long-acting injectables not fully addressed by the rule; enforcement gaps for existing PrEP UM prohibition; inadequate granularity in proposed metrics reporting.

---

## 8. SUPPORTING EVIDENCE

- **Data or statistics cited:** ~1.2 million people in the US living with HIV (~half covered by affected payers); ~2.3 million may benefit from PrEP; 20% greater HIV acquisition risk within 12 months from 1–7 day PrEP dispensing delay (retrospective analysis of 500,000+ PrEP prescriptions, IDWeek 2023 poster); six states (CO, LA, NV, NY, TX, OR) have enacted ARV PA/step therapy prohibitions.
- **Studies or research referenced:** Tao L et al., IDWeek 2023 (PrEP dispensing delay and HIV acquisition risk); Nguyen E et al., Current Medical Research and Opinion 2016 (systematic review of 29 studies on non-medical switching in stable disease); Severe P et al., NEJM 2010 (early vs. standard ART in Haiti); Kitahata MM et al., NEJM 2009 (early vs. deferred ART survival); D'Angelo A et al., Health Affairs Aug 2025 (insurance denials and cost-sharing for PrEP among sexual and gender minority people); KFF data on HIV insurance coverage and Medicaid.
- **Examples provided:** HHS Guidelines recommending immediate ART initiation after diagnosis; six state laws prohibiting ARV PA/step therapy; long-acting injectables (cabotegravir/rilpivirine) billed under pharmacy or medical benefit depending on payer causing wrong-benefit rejections.

---

## 9. IMPACT ASSESSMENT

- **Affected stakeholders:** ~600,000 people with HIV covered by affected payers; ~2.3 million potential PrEP users; sexual and gender minority populations; ViiV Healthcare as ARV/PrEP manufacturer
- **Economic implications:** Not directly addressed; notes cost-sharing violations where PrEP lab services should be covered at no cost
- **Technical feasibility:** Flags the need for medical benefit PA APIs to add real-time coverage check capability (analogous to RTPB for pharmacy benefit) — a new technical requirement not in current rule; automatic claim rerouting requires payer system enhancements
- **Patient care impact:** Very high — PA/step therapy barriers for HIV treatment documented to increase morbidity, mortality, and transmission; even brief PrEP dispensing delays increase HIV acquisition risk by 20%

---

## 10. SENTIMENT ANALYSIS

- **Overall position:** Supportive (with targeted strengthening requests focused on HIV/PrEP access)
- **Tone:** Professional, evidence-based, advocacy-oriented
- **Priority level:** High (public health implications; detailed evidence base; HIV epidemic end-strategy alignment)

---

## 11. KEY QUOTES

1. "For people with HIV, the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) Guidelines for the Use of Antiretroviral Agents in Adults and Adolescents with HIV recommend that a person with HIV initiate ART 'immediately (or as soon as possible) after diagnosis.'" — Context: Justifying a uniform 24-hour timeframe and no extensions for ARV PA.

2. "A recent retrospective analysis of more than half a million individuals who were prescribed PrEP found that delayed dispensing of 1 to 7 days compared to same-day dispensing led to a 20% greater chance of acquiring HIV within 12 months." — Context: Evidence base for prohibiting timeframe extensions for PrEP.

3. "Utilization management, however, can prevent rapid access to the most clinically appropriate treatments for people newly diagnosed with HIV... delays in access to treatment can have adverse consequences for individual and public health." — Context: Central argument for extending Part D ARV protections to all CMS markets.

4. "Many issuers and plans continue to inappropriately apply prior authorization to PrEP and ancillary services and must be stopped." — Context: Urging enforcement of existing Tri-Department FAQ Part 68 prohibition.

---

## 12. THEMES

- [x] **PATIENT-ACCESS** — Core theme: PA, step therapy, and benefit routing barriers directly delay HIV treatment and PrEP access with documented individual and public health consequences including increased HIV transmission risk.
- [x] **HEALTH-EQUITY** — HIV patients and PrEP users — disproportionately sexual and gender minority people — face compounded barriers from utilization management violations; six states have enacted protections ViiV urges CMS to adopt federally.
- [x] **TRANSPARENCY** — Urges granular PA metrics disaggregation (by drug, therapeutic area, denial reason, plan type) to enable monitoring of disproportionate impacts on HIV patients and payer gaming behavior.
- [x] **MEDICAL-VS-PHARMACY-BENEFIT** — Specifically addresses wrong-benefit rejections for long-acting injectable ARVs; urges real-time benefit routing information and automatic claim rerouting.
- [x] **EXISTING-WORKFLOWS** — Flags that long-acting injectables span benefit categories in ways current PA workflows don't accommodate; advocates for real-time coverage checks on the medical benefit side analogous to RTPB on pharmacy side.
- [x] **STANDARDS-MATURITY** — Implicitly: medical benefit PA APIs should be expanded to support patient-specific real-time coverage checks — a capability not yet required by the rule.
- [x] **IMPLEMENTATION-TIMELINE** — Not a primary concern; ViiV supports finalization and urges stronger, not delayed, requirements.
- [x] **REGULATORY-AUTHORITY** — Urges CMS to use its authority across all regulated markets to prohibit ARV utilization management; calls for enforcement of existing Tri-Department FAQ Part 68 guidance.
